question: What is the primary purpose of isolation in healthcare settings?

options.A: To punish patients who refuse medication
options.C: To provide private rooms for wealthy patients
options.D: To separate infected patients and stop disease spread

explanation: Isolation physically separates contagious patients to prevent pathogens from spreading to others in the hospital environment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h1)

question: A patient with suspected Lassa fever is placed in a single room away from others. This action demonstrates what concept?
explanation: Placing a known or suspected infectious patient apart from others to prevent transmission is the definition of isolation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h1)

question: Isolation precautions primarily interrupt which link in the chain of infection?
explanation: Barriers like gloves, masks, and private rooms block the way pathogens travel from person to person. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: Breaking the chain of infection using physical barriers protects which group most directly?
explanation: Stopping transmission prevents vulnerable individuals from acquiring the infectious agent. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: Standard precautions must be used with which category of patients?

options.D: Patients admitted to surgical wards only

explanation: Standard precautions form the baseline level of infection control for every patient interaction, regardless of diagnosis. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: A nurse wears gloves before touching a patient's intact skin during a routine bath. Why is this practice incorrect under standard precautions?

options.A: Gloves make the patient feel stigmatized and unwelcome
options.B: Gloves prevent the nurse from performing proper hand hygiene
options.C: Gloves are only required when touching blood or body fluids, not intact skin
options.D: Gloves must be changed every two minutes during bathing

explanation: Standard precautions dictate that gloves are worn for touching blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, and non-intact skin, but not routine care on intact skin. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: What type of room is required for a patient placed on airborne precautions?

options.D: Open ward bed near a window

explanation: Negative pressure rooms prevent contaminated air from flowing out into the hallway when the door opens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: A patient with pulmonary tuberculosis needs which specific respiratory protection for healthcare workers entering the room?
explanation: Airborne pathogens like tuberculosis require high-filtration respirators to filter out tiny infectious droplet nuclei. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: What is the first item of PPE that should be removed during doffing?
explanation: Gloves are considered the most contaminated item and are removed first to avoid spreading pathogens to other parts of the body. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why is the mask removed last when taking off full personal protective equipment?

options.A: Because masks are the cleanest item and do not require disposal
options.B: To prevent inhaling infectious particles during the removal process
options.C: Because masks are difficult to untie with wet hands
options.D: To allow the nurse to speak clearly to the patient

explanation: Keeping the respiratory protection on until the end ensures accidental pathogen inhalation is blocked while handling contaminated garments. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why should dedicated medical equipment remain inside an isolation room?

options.A: To make it easier for the doctor to find instruments
options.B: To keep the nursing station clean and uncluttered
options.C: To prevent carrying pathogens out to other patients
options.D: To reduce the cost of buying hospital stethoscopes

explanation: Using dedicated equipment stops fomites from transferring infectious agents from an isolated patient to others. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h6)

question: A nurse bundles medication administration, dressing changes, and vital sign checks into one room entry. What is the primary benefit of this action?

options.B: Accelerating the patient's physical recovery time
options.C: Conserving PPE and reducing exposure frequency
options.D: Complying with hospital visiting hour policies

explanation: Combining tasks limits how many times staff enter the room, saving protective gear and lowering infection risk. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h6)

question: A patient in strict isolation refuses to eat and cries frequently. What nursing intervention is most appropriate?

options.A: Request an immediate psychiatric admission for depression
options.B: Reassure the patient that isolation is temporary and leave them alone
options.C: Spend time communicating at the doorway and provide reading materials
options.D: Remove the isolation sign so family members can visit freely

explanation: Regular communication and engagement reduce feelings of abandonment while maintaining infection control boundaries. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: Which psychological response is commonly observed in patients undergoing prolonged isolation?
explanation: Sensory deprivation and lack of physical touch frequently lead to low mood and emotional distress in isolated patients. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: Reporting a suspected outbreak of a communicable disease is primarily the responsibility of whom?
explanation: Nurses monitor patient conditions closely and must report unusual disease clusters to prompt infection control action. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h8)

question: A nurse notices a visitor entering an isolation room without putting on a gown. What action should the nurse take?

options.A: Wait until the visitor leaves before mentioning anything
options.B: Report the visitor to hospital security immediately
options.C: Ignore the action since visitors are not clinical staff
options.D: Politely stop the visitor and explain the required PPE steps

explanation: Nurses are responsible for enforcing safety protocols with all individuals entering isolation environments. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h8)
